**Other information:**

Adds `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/IconColumns.spec.mjs`, which pins `applyRecordConfigs(config, record)` of the `Icon`, `IconLink` and `LinkedIn` grid columns. It follows the setup of `Component.spec.mjs` and uses a plain object as the record. No file under `src/` is changed: all three columns agree with every row of the table in the issue.

One `test(...)` per table row, nine in total:

| Column | Test |
|---|---|
| `Icon` | uses the record value as cellIconCls when the column has none |
| `Icon` | uses a fixed cellIconCls from the column |
| `IconLink` | passes the record value through without formatters |
| `IconLink` | builds the url with urlFormatter |
| `IconLink` | builds the label with labelFormatter |
| `LinkedIn` | builds the profile url from a bare handle |
| `LinkedIn` | keeps a value starting with http as it is |
| `LinkedIn` | defaults cellIconCls to the LinkedIn brand icon |
| all three | a key passed in config wins over the derived one |

Notes:

- The formatter tests also check the arguments: `urlFormatter(value, record)` and `labelFormatter(x, record)` get the same record object, and `x` is the `labelField` value when one is set, else the record value.
- To check that the tests can fail, I temporarily broke each column locally (dropped the trailing `/` of the LinkedIn URL, inverted `hidden` in `Icon`, passed the wrong value to `labelFormatter`): 4 of the 9 tests failed. Those changes are not part of this PR.

Verification (Windows 11, Node 25.8.1):

- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/column/IconColumns.spec.mjs`: 9 passed
- `npm run test-unit`: 4720 passed, 49 failed. The same 49 tests fail on my machine on `dev` without this file (4711 passed, 49 failed), so the difference is the 9 new tests. The failures are mostly in `buildScripts` specs, none under `grid/`, and look Windows-related (for example a path built as `C:\C:\Users\...` and `spawnSync npm ENOENT`). I can open a separate issue with the list if that is useful.

AI use, as asked in CONTRIBUTING.md section 5: written with the help of Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed the tests and ran them locally.
